sudan.title: مستجدات الشرق الأوسط: أكثر من 100 قتيل في هجمات بالمسيرات في أنحاء السودان - SBS
sudan.summary: أفادت التقارير أن أكثر من 100 شخص لقوا حتفهم في سلسلة من الهجمات التي نفذتها طائرات مسيرة في مختلف أنحاء السودان. تأتي هذه الهجمات في وقت يشهد فيه البلد تصاعدًا في النزاع المسلح، حيث تتزايد الاشتباكات بين القوات الحكومية والمجموعات المسلحة. وقد أدت هذه الأحداث إلى تفاقم الأوضاع الإنسانية في البلاد، مع تزايد أعداد النازحين والجرحى. كما دعت منظمات حقوق الإنسان إلى ضرورة اتخاذ إجراءات عاجلة لحماية المدنيين وتقديم المساعدات اللازمة للمتضررين من هذه الهجمات.

sudan.title: السودان: أكثر من 100 قتيل في هجمات بمسيّرات على كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم - France 24
sudan.summary: أفادت تقارير أن أكثر من 100 شخص لقوا حتفهم في هجمات شنتها طائرات مسيّرة في مناطق كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم بالسودان. الهجمات، التي تُعتبر من بين الأكثر دموية في الصراع المستمر في البلاد، استهدفت مدنيين وأدت إلى تدمير العديد من المنازل والبنية التحتية. وقد أثارت هذه الأحداث قلقاً دولياً متزايداً بشأن الوضع الإنساني في السودان، حيث يعاني السكان من نقص حاد في المساعدات الأساسية. الحكومة السودانية لم تصدر بعد بياناً رسمياً حول هذه الهجمات، لكن المنظمات الإنسانية تدعو إلى اتخاذ إجراءات عاجلة لحماية المدنيين وتقديم المساعدة للمحتاجين.

sudan.title: وزير الصحة يشارك في مؤتمر وجائزة ميدغلوبال بشيكاغو - سودان اندبندنت
sudan.summary: شارك وزير الصحة في مؤتمر وجائزة ميدغلوبال الذي أقيم في شيكاغو، حيث تم مناقشة قضايا الصحة العالمية والتحديات التي تواجهها الدول. المؤتمر جمع خبراء وصناع قرار من مختلف أنحاء العالم لتبادل الأفكار والخبرات في مجال الرعاية الصحية. كما تم تسليط الضوء على الابتكارات والحلول الممكنة لتحسين الخدمات الصحية. الوزير أعرب عن أهمية التعاون الدولي في مواجهة الأوبئة والأمراض المزمنة، وأكد على التزام السودان بتحسين النظام الصحي وتوفير الرعاية اللازمة للمواطنين.

sudan.title: مجلس الأمن والدفاع يوجه بالتصدي للمخططات المهددة للبلاد - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: عقد مجلس الأمن والدفاع في السودان اجتماعًا لمناقشة التهديدات التي تواجه البلاد، حيث تم توجيه الجهات المعنية بالتصدي للمخططات التي تهدد الأمن القومي. وركز الاجتماع على التحديات الأمنية والسياسية التي يواجهها السودان، بما في ذلك الأزمات الداخلية والنزاعات. كما تم التأكيد على أهمية تعزيز التعاون بين القوات المسلحة والأجهزة الأمنية لضمان استقرار البلاد. وأشار المجلس إلى ضرورة اتخاذ إجراءات فورية لمواجهة هذه التهديدات وحماية المواطنين.

sudan.title: جوبا تستدعي السفير السوداني احتجاجًا على قصف سوق «النعام» في أبيي - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: استدعت حكومة جوبا السفير السوداني احتجاجًا على القصف الذي استهدف سوق «النعام» في منطقة أبيي. وأعربت وزارة الخارجية في جنوب السودان عن إدانتها الشديدة لهذا الهجوم، الذي أسفر عن وقوع إصابات وأضرار مادية. وأكدت الحكومة أنها ستتخذ إجراءات دبلوماسية مناسبة للتعامل مع هذا الاعتداء، مشددة على أهمية الحفاظ على الأمن والاستقرار في المنطقة. يأتي هذا التصعيد في ظل التوترات المستمرة بين السودان وجنوب السودان، حيث تسعى جوبا إلى تعزيز العلاقات مع جيرانها وتفادي أي تصعيد عسكري.

sudan.title: السودان: أكثر من 100 قتيل في غارات بمسيّرات على كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم - Euronews.com
sudan.summary: أسفرت غارات جوية باستخدام مسيّرات عن مقتل أكثر من 100 شخص في مناطق كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم بالسودان. وتأتي هذه الهجمات في وقت يشهد فيه البلد تصاعدًا في النزاع المسلح بين القوات الحكومية والمجموعات المسلحة. وقد أدت الغارات إلى تدمير العديد من المنازل والبنية التحتية، مما زاد من معاناة المدنيين. كما تم الإبلاغ عن إصابة العشرات، مما يفاقم من الوضع الإنساني المتدهور في البلاد. وتستمر الدعوات الدولية لوقف الأعمال العدائية وتقديم المساعدات الإنسانية للمتضررين.

sudan.title: ذهب السودان المنهوب في الإمارات – الشروق أونلاين - الشروق أونلاين
sudan.summary: تتناول المقالة قضية الذهب المنهوب من السودان الذي يُهرّب إلى الإمارات. تشير التقارير إلى أن كميات كبيرة من الذهب تُستخرج بشكل غير قانوني في السودان، حيث تستفيد من ذلك شبكات تهريب منظمة. يُعتقد أن هذه الشبكات تعمل بالتعاون مع بعض الجهات في الإمارات، مما يسهل عملية التهريب ويعزز من تجارة الذهب غير المشروعة. يُظهر الوضع القائم كيف أن الفساد وضعف الرقابة في السودان يسهمان في تفشي هذه الظاهرة، مما يؤدي إلى فقدان البلاد لعائدات كبيرة من مواردها الطبيعية. كما تثير القضية تساؤلات حول دور الإمارات في هذه الأنشطة وكيفية تأثيرها على الاقتصاد السوداني.

sudan.title: لجنة المعلمين تعلن إضرابًا شاملًا في الخرطوم يومي الأربعاء والخميس - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: أعلنت لجنة المعلمين في السودان عن إضراب شامل في العاصمة الخرطوم يومي الأربعاء والخميس القادمين. يأتي هذا الإضراب احتجاجًا على الأوضاع الحالية في قطاع التعليم، بما في ذلك نقص الموارد والظروف المعيشية الصعبة التي يواجهها المعلمون. وأكدت اللجنة أن الإضراب يهدف إلى الضغط على الحكومة لتحسين أوضاع المعلمين وتوفير بيئة تعليمية مناسبة للطلاب. كما دعت اللجنة جميع المعلمين إلى الالتزام بالإضراب والمشاركة في الفعاليات المقررة خلال هذه الأيام.

sudan.title: هجومان بالمسيّرات في السودان.. 80 قتيلا بغرب كردفان و4 آخرون قرب مطار الخرطوم - الجزيرة نت
sudan.summary: شنّت هجمات بطائرات مسيّرة في السودان، أسفرت عن مقتل 80 شخصًا في منطقة غرب كردفان، بالإضافة إلى 4 آخرين بالقرب من مطار الخرطوم. تأتي هذه الهجمات في وقت يشهد فيه السودان تصاعدًا في النزاع المسلح بين القوات الحكومية ومجموعات مسلحة. وقد أدت هذه الأحداث إلى تفاقم الأوضاع الإنسانية في البلاد، حيث يعاني السكان من نقص حاد في الإمدادات الأساسية. السلطات المحلية دعت إلى تقديم المساعدات العاجلة للمتضررين من هذه الهجمات، وسط مخاوف من استمرار العنف وزيادة عدد الضحايا.

sudan.title: خريطة حرائق الغابات في Sinnar - IQAir
sudan.summary: تظهر خريطة حرائق الغابات في ولاية سنار، التي تم إعدادها بواسطة IQAir، انتشار الحرائق وتأثيرها على جودة الهواء في المنطقة. تُظهر البيانات أن الحرائق تؤثر بشكل كبير على البيئة، مما يؤدي إلى تدهور جودة الهواء وزيادة المخاطر الصحية للسكان. يُنصح السكان باتخاذ الاحتياطات اللازمة، مثل تجنب الأنشطة الخارجية واستخدام الكمامات، خاصة في المناطق الأكثر تضرراً. تسلط الخريطة الضوء على أهمية الوعي البيئي والتدخل السريع للحد من آثار هذه الحرائق.

ethiopia.title: Nile and Red Sea Inseparable Pillars Capable of Creating Regional Cooperation, Integration: Researchers - ENA English
ethiopia.summary: Researchers have emphasized the interconnectedness of the Nile and Red Sea as vital components for fostering regional cooperation and integration in East Africa. They argue that these two bodies of water are not only crucial for the ecological and economic stability of the region but also serve as platforms for collaborative initiatives among neighboring countries. By leveraging the resources and strategic significance of the Nile and Red Sea, nations can enhance trade, address environmental challenges, and promote sustainable development. The researchers advocate for a unified approach to managing these waterways, highlighting the potential benefits of regional partnerships in achieving long-term stability and prosperity.

ethiopia.title: Can diplomacy prevent an Ethiopia-Eritrea war as Tigray gets a new administration? - DW.com
ethiopia.summary: As Ethiopia establishes a new administration in the Tigray region, concerns are rising about potential conflict with Eritrea. The recent political changes in Tigray could exacerbate tensions between the two nations, particularly given their historical animosities and the ongoing humanitarian crisis in the region. Diplomatic efforts are being called upon to mitigate the risk of war, with international stakeholders urging dialogue and cooperation. Analysts emphasize the importance of addressing underlying issues to foster stability and peace. The situation remains precarious, and the effectiveness of diplomatic interventions will be crucial in preventing escalation into armed conflict.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia’s Naval Experience Contributes to Red Sea Security: Aregawi Berhe - ENA English
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia's naval experience is playing a significant role in enhancing security in the Red Sea, according to Aregawi Berhe, the Director-General of the Ethiopian Maritime Affairs Authority. He emphasized that Ethiopia's strategic position and its commitment to maritime security are crucial for regional stability. The country has been actively involved in collaborative efforts with neighboring nations to address security challenges in the Red Sea, including piracy and illegal fishing. Aregawi highlighted the importance of building a capable navy and fostering partnerships to ensure safe navigation and protect maritime resources. Ethiopia's engagement in maritime security reflects its broader goals of contributing to peace and stability in the region.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia's national security imperative: Alliance with Israel and Somaliland - The Jerusalem Post
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia is strengthening its national security by forging alliances with Israel and Somaliland. This strategic partnership aims to enhance military cooperation and intelligence sharing, addressing regional threats and instability. The collaboration with Israel is particularly significant, as it provides Ethiopia with advanced technology and expertise in counter-terrorism efforts. Meanwhile, the alliance with Somaliland is focused on bolstering security in the Horn of Africa, where Ethiopia faces challenges from various militant groups. These alliances are seen as essential for Ethiopia to safeguard its interests and maintain stability in a volatile region. The Ethiopian government emphasizes that these partnerships will contribute to a more secure and prosperous future for the nation.

ethiopia.title: Crisis in Central Ethiopia: 11 Dead as Armed Raids Devastate East Gurage - EthiopiaToday
ethiopia.summary: In East Gurage, Central Ethiopia, armed raids have resulted in the deaths of 11 individuals, exacerbating an ongoing crisis in the region. The violence has led to widespread fear and displacement among local communities. Authorities are struggling to maintain order as tensions rise, with reports of increased attacks and retaliatory violence. The situation has drawn attention from humanitarian organizations, which are concerned about the safety and well-being of affected populations. Efforts to restore peace and provide assistance are underway, but challenges remain significant as the conflict continues to escalate. The government has been urged to take decisive action to address the root causes of the violence and protect civilians.

ethiopia.title: News: Ethiopia warns Somaliland recognition could strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland officials push back - Addis Standard
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia has issued a warning that recognizing Somaliland as an independent state could bolster the influence of Al-Shabaab, the militant group operating in the region. Ethiopian officials argue that such recognition might destabilize the Horn of Africa and exacerbate security challenges. In response, Somaliland officials have pushed back against this assertion, emphasizing their desire for international recognition and asserting that their independence would not contribute to the strengthening of Al-Shabaab. They argue that Somaliland has maintained relative peace and stability compared to the rest of Somalia. The ongoing debate highlights the complex geopolitical dynamics in the region, as various stakeholders weigh the implications of Somaliland's quest for recognition against the backdrop of security concerns.

ethiopia.title: Alliance for Survival rejects Rubio’s characterization of #Ethiopia’s conflict as separatist, terrorist - Facebook
ethiopia.summary: The Alliance for Survival has rejected Senator Marco Rubio's characterization of the conflict in Ethiopia as separatist and terrorist in nature. The group argues that such labels misrepresent the complexities of the situation and undermine the legitimate grievances of various communities involved in the conflict. They emphasize that the ongoing violence is rooted in deeper political and social issues rather than a simple separatist agenda. The Alliance calls for a more nuanced understanding of the conflict and urges for dialogue and peaceful resolution rather than the use of inflammatory rhetoric. They stress the importance of addressing the underlying causes of the unrest to achieve lasting peace in the region.

ethiopia.title: Airbus Projects Sixfold Growth in Ethiopia's Air Passenger Traffic Over Next 20 Years
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Airbus Projects Sixfold Growth in Ethiopia's Air Passenger Traffic Over Next 20 Years - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Airbus Projects Sixfold Growth in Ethiopia's Air Passenger Traffic Over Next 20 Years 19 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Airbus has forecast a sixfold rise in Ethiopia's air passenger traffic over the next 20 years, saying Ethiopian Airlines is well placed to turn Addis Ababa into one of Africa's leading aviation hubs. It cited Ethiopian Airlines' expanding network, growing demand and planned airport infrastructure as key factors positioning Addis Ababa to become a leading aviation hub in Africa Airbus Vice President for Market Analysis and Forecast Antonio Da Costa told ENA that Ethiopia has strong growth potential, with Ethiopian Airlines well positioned to capitalize on rising passenger numbers and expanding regional and international connectivity. "We're obviously extremely proud to be a partner of Ethiopian Airlines," Da Costa said. "Ethiopian Airlines are our first A350 customer in Africa and have been a great customer of the 350 over the last 10 years." Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Da Costa said the airline's established network, fleet capabilities and hub strategy would help it accommodate the projected increase in passenger traffic. "We obviously see a very good and strong potential of growth in Ethiopia with over six times more passengers coming over the next 20 years," he said. "So we believe that Ethiopian Airlines is well placed to cover and to take advantage of that growth." Airbus also projects that African air traffic will triple over the same period, creating opportunities for airlines and airports to expand capacity and strengthen connections across the continent and beyond. Da Costa said Addis Ababa's role in African aviation would become increasingly significant as Ethiopia develops its planned airport infrastructure, including the new airport project in Bishoftu. Ethiopia has described the Bishoftu airport project as the largest aviation infrastructure undertaking in Africa's history. Upon completion and full operation, the airport is expected to accommodate up to 110 million passengers annually and serve as Ethiopian Airlines' principal operating base. "We expect that Addis Ababa and with the new airport to become more and more a central hub for the traffic in Africa," Da Costa said. "We expect that growth of trans-African traffic for the Ethiopian coverage will be increasing by about six times over the next 20 years." Ethiopian Airlines became the first African operator of the Airbus A350 in 2016 and subsequently became the first African customer for the larger A350-1000, strengthening its position in the continent's long-haul aviation market. Da Costa described Ethiopian Airlines as a historic African carrier and reaffirmed Airbus's commitment to supporting its expansion with modern, fuel-efficient aircraft suited to its growing operational needs. "As we want to continue to grow with new aircraft, better aircraft, we're always open to hear from Ethiopian Airlines what their needs are," he said. "We will do our utmost to make sure that we can provide the best aircraft to serve the growing needs of the airline." He noted that connecting passengers account for nearly two-thirds of Ethiopian Airlines' traffic, highlighting Addis Ababa's importance as a transfer point linking destinations across Africa with Europe, Asia, the Americas and other international markets. "We're delighted that we have aircraft like the A350 that is capable of connecting Addis Ababa to effectively the whole world," Da Costa said. "By doing so, we believe that we're providing Ethiopian Airlines with the right tools to continue this strong growth." He added that Airbus would continue working with Ethiopian Airlines to provide aircraft, technical support and operational solutions to help the carrier expand efficiently and sustainably as demand for air travel increases. The projected growth would further strengthen Ethiopia's ambitions to consolidate its position as a major gateway for African aviation, while the planned airport infrastructure is expected to provide additional capacity to support the airline's long-term expansion. ethiopia.summary: Airbus has projected a sixfold increase in Ethiopia's air passenger traffic over the next 20 years, highlighting Ethiopian Airlines' potential to establish Addis Ababa as a major aviation hub in Africa. Key factors contributing to this growth include the airline's expanding network, rising demand, and planned airport infrastructure, particularly the new airport project in Bishoftu, which aims to accommodate up to 110 million passengers annually. Airbus Vice President Antonio Da Costa emphasized the airline's strong position to leverage this growth, noting that Ethiopian Airlines has been a significant customer for Airbus, including being the first African operator of the A350. The anticipated growth in Ethiopian air traffic aligns with Airbus's forecast of a tripling of air traffic across Africa, enhancing the continent's connectivity and capacity.

ethiopia.title: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead George Appiah/Wikimedia Commons The Independence Arch in Accra represents Ghana’s democracy. 19 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Ghana is projected to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to reach US$128.64 billion, exceeding Ethiopia's projected US$127.15 billion by US$1.49 billion, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), as reported by African Business Insider on 17 October. The projected shift comes after Kenya overtook Ethiopia as East Africa's largest economy in nominal US dollar terms, marking another change in the continent's economic rankings driven partly by exchange-rate movements rather than differences in real economic growth. The IMF's latest estimates place Ghana eighth among Africa's largest economies, ahead of Ethiopia in ninth place and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose economy is projected at US$122.28 billion. While Ghana's nominal GDP is expected to edge ahead of Ethiopia's, the two countries have markedly different growth forecasts. Ethiopia's economy is projected to expand by 9.2% in real terms in 2026, compared with Ghana's forecast growth of 5.7%. However, the depreciation of the Ethiopian birr following the government's July 2024 foreign-exchange reforms has reduced the dollar value of the country's economic output, narrowing its position in nominal GDP rankings despite strong projected domestic growth. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Ghana's recovery and economic position Ghana's projected rise comes as the West African country continues to recover from a severe financial crisis marked by currency depreciation, high inflation, mounting public debt and pressure on government finances. In 2023, Ghana secured a US$3 billion IMF support programme aimed at restoring macroeconomic stability, addressing debt vulnerabilities and rebuilding investor confidence. The government subsequently pursued fiscal reforms, debt restructuring and measures to stabilise prices and the national currency. The country's economic position is also supported by exports of gold, cocoa, oil and gas, alongside financial services and a growing consumer market. Gold remains a major source of export earnings and foreign exchange, with higher international prices providing additional support to inflows. However, an improved position in nominal GDP rankings does not necessarily translate into higher living standards or stronger productive capacity. Sustaining the recovery will depend on Ghana's ability to attract long-term investment, create employment and expand industrial production. Ethiopia's growth versus dollar-denominated output Ethiopia's projected position reflects the distinction between real economic growth and nominal GDP measured in US dollars. While real GDP growth captures changes in domestic production after accounting for price changes, nominal GDP expressed in dollars is also affected by inflation and movements in the exchange rate. The depreciation of the birr following Ethiopia's July 2024 shift toward a more market-determined foreign-exchange system substantially reduced the dollar valuation of its output. The reform formed part of the government's broader economic programme, supported by an approximately US$3.4 billion IMF Extended Credit Facility. As Addis Standard reported last week, Kenya's emergence as East Africa's largest economy in dollar terms was similarly shaped by exchange-rate movements, with the comparatively stronger performance of the Kenyan shilling increasing the dollar value of its economic output. The IMF's October projections indicate that Ethiopia's economy is expected to grow by 9.2% in 2026 and 7.8% in 2027, while Kenya's growth is forecast at 4.5% and 4.7%, respectively. The figures highlight how an economy can record faster real growth without maintaining a higher ranking when GDP is measured in US dollars. The projected shift involving Ghana therefore does not, by itself, establish that its underlying economy is growing faster than Ethiopia's. Rather, it underscores the influence of exchange-rate movements and macroeconomic conditions on the relative dollar value of African economies. However, its October WEO, titled Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices, warns that high debt-servicing costs, limited foreign-exchange reserves and declining aid are constraining governments' ability to respond to economic shocks. For Ethiopia, the projected change in Africa's economic rankings highlights the challenge of sustaining rapid domestic growth while managing currency pressures, inflation and foreign-exchange constraints. For Ghana, moving ahead in nominal GDP terms would mark a recovery in its relative economic position, but translating that ranking into lasting gains in investment, employment and industrial development remains a separate challenge. ethiopia.summary: Ghana is projected to surpass Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with an estimated GDP of $128.64 billion compared to Ethiopia's $127.15 billion, according to the IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook. This shift follows Kenya's recent emergence as East Africa's largest economy. While Ghana's nominal GDP is set to increase, Ethiopia is expected to experience a higher real growth rate of 9.2%, compared to Ghana's 5.7%. The depreciation of the Ethiopian birr has impacted its dollar-denominated GDP, despite strong domestic growth. Ghana's recovery from a financial crisis, supported by a $3 billion IMF program, is driven by exports and fiscal reforms. However, the change in nominal GDP rankings does not necessarily reflect improved living standards or economic capacity, highlighting the influence of exchange rates and macroeconomic conditions on economic measurements.

ethiopia.title: Alliance for Survival Rejects Rubio's Characterization of Ethiopia's Conflict As Separatist, Terrorist
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Alliance for Survival Rejects Rubio's Characterization of Ethiopia's Conflict As Separatist, Terrorist - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Alliance for Survival Rejects Rubio's Characterization of Ethiopia's Conflict As Separatist, Terrorist © RFI/Noé Hochet-Bodin The primary school in Erebti, Ethiopia, was bombed and destroyed during clashes between Tigrayan TPLF rebels and regional militiamen on May 4, 2022. 19 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — The Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival (Alliance for Survival), a coalition of armed and political groups opposing the federal government, has rejected remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterizing aspects of Ethiopia's conflict as separatist and terrorist, calling on Washington to adopt what it described as a balanced approach to the conflict. In a statement issued on 18 October, the alliance said its military operations were not driven by separatist objectives or intended to fragment the country. Instead, it described its actions as self-defense after what it called the government's rejection of efforts to achieve a peaceful resolution, including through the November 2022 Pretoria Agreement. The alliance said its stated objective was to facilitate an inclusive democratic transition, restore peace and stability, and allow Ethiopians to determine the country's political future. It also rejected the characterization of its attacks on government military installations as terrorism, arguing that such descriptions misrepresented the conflict. The alliance accused government forces of using more advanced weapons against both military targets and densely populated civilian areas in territories under its control. Addis Standard could not independently verify the allegations. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The statement warned that such characterizations could encourage the government to continue its military campaign and undermine efforts to resolve the conflict peacefully. The alliance urged the United States to adopt what it called a balanced and constructive position to support a lasting peace in Ethiopia. The statement follows Rubio's remarks on the conflict in Ethiopia during an interview with C-SPAN. The Alliance for Survival brings together several armed and political groups opposed to the federal government, including the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), the Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM), and other groups from different regions. Its formation was announced in September amid renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia. Rubio's remarks come amid continued clashes between federal government forces and armed groups affiliated with the Alliance for Survival across multiple fronts in northern Ethiopia and other parts of the country. On 24 September 2026, Addis Standard reported that the European Union had expressed concern over the formation of a new coalition of Ethiopian opposition and armed groups, warning of a deteriorating security situation in northern Ethiopia and its impact on civilians. The EU said it was "deeply concerned by the rapidly deteriorating situation in Northern Ethiopia and its impact on the population," citing reports of military activity across multiple localities. It called for "immediate de-escalation" and urged the parties to recommit to the November 2022 Permanent Cessation of Hostilities Agreement, signed in Pretoria between the federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). The EU stressed that differences between the parties could "only be resolved through dialogue and not military action" and called for compliance with international humanitarian law, emphasizing the obligation to protect civilians and safeguard the impartiality and independence of humanitarian operations. The coalition, initially announced as the Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Coalition for Survival, was formally unveiled on 20 September in a statement read live on Tigrai TV by Zemene Kassie , chairman of the Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM). Seven opposition and armed groups declared a shared objective of removing the Prosperity Party-led government and establishing an inclusive transitional administration. The coalition comprises the AFNM, the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), the TPLF, the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF), the Afar National Unity Revolutionary Front, the Benishangul Peoples' Liberation Movement, and the Gumuz Peoples' Democratic Movement. The announcement followed months of reported efforts to coordinate opposition groups across regional and political lines. In August, Zemene said agreements had been reached with several armed opposition groups to establish a broader alliance aimed at the "fall of Abiy Ahmed." The September announcement gave the emerging alignment a formal name and publicly stated its political objectives. Read the original article on Addis Standard . ethiopia.summary: The Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival has rejected U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's characterization of the ongoing conflict in Ethiopia as separatist and terrorist. In a statement on October 18, the alliance, which includes various armed and political groups opposing the federal government, asserted that its military actions are acts of self-defense rather than attempts to fragment the country. They emphasized their goal of facilitating an inclusive democratic transition and restoring peace, while criticizing the government's military tactics against civilians. The alliance urged the U.S. to adopt a balanced approach to the conflict, warning that mischaracterizations could hinder peaceful resolutions. The statement follows Rubio's comments during a C-SPAN interview amid ongoing clashes between federal forces and the alliance's members across northern Ethiopia.

somalia.title: Families fleeing Somalia crises find bleak prospects in Dadaab refugee camps - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: Families fleeing crises in Somalia are facing dire conditions in the Dadaab refugee camps in Kenya. The camps, originally established to accommodate a temporary influx of refugees, are now home to over 200,000 people, leading to overcrowding and limited resources. Many refugees are struggling with inadequate access to food, clean water, and healthcare. The ongoing conflict, drought, and famine in Somalia have driven families to seek safety, but the camps offer little hope for a better future. Aid organizations are overwhelmed and unable to meet the growing needs of the population, leaving many refugees in a state of uncertainty and despair. The situation highlights the urgent need for international support and sustainable solutions to address the challenges faced by displaced families.

somalia.title: Somalia aviation authority, IATA sign agreement to strengthen safety oversight - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: The Somalia Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA) has signed a significant agreement with the International Air Transport Association (IATA) aimed at enhancing safety oversight in the country's aviation sector. This partnership is expected to improve regulatory frameworks and operational standards, ultimately fostering a safer flying environment in Somalia. The agreement includes provisions for training and capacity-building initiatives for local aviation personnel, ensuring compliance with international safety standards. The collaboration reflects Somalia's commitment to developing its aviation industry and enhancing air travel safety, which is crucial for economic growth and connectivity in the region.

somalia.title: Libya and Somalia Discuss Economic and Trade Cooperation - Libya Herald
somalia.summary: Libya and Somalia have engaged in discussions to enhance economic and trade cooperation between the two nations. The talks focused on potential partnerships in various sectors, aiming to boost bilateral trade and investment. Both countries expressed a commitment to strengthening their economic ties and exploring opportunities for collaboration. The discussions are part of broader efforts to foster regional cooperation and development. Officials from both sides highlighted the importance of sharing resources and expertise to achieve mutual benefits. The meetings reflect a growing interest in establishing stronger economic relationships within the region.

somalia.title: Somalia beat Rwanda on penalties to reach CECAFA U-17 final - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: Somalia triumphed over Rwanda in a tense penalty shootout to secure a place in the CECAFA U-17 final. The match ended in a draw after regulation and extra time, leading to penalties where Somalia emerged victorious. This win marks a significant achievement for the Somali U-17 team, showcasing their resilience and skill in a competitive tournament. The final will see Somalia compete for the championship title, further highlighting the progress of youth football in the region.

somalia.title: Anticipatory Action Implementation Plan Somalia - Floods - ReliefWeb
somalia.summary: The Anticipatory Action Implementation Plan for Somalia addresses the increasing risk of floods in the region, aiming to enhance preparedness and response strategies. The plan outlines proactive measures to mitigate the impact of flooding on vulnerable communities, emphasizing timely interventions and resource allocation. It focuses on early warning systems, community engagement, and collaboration with local authorities to ensure effective implementation. The initiative seeks to reduce the humanitarian consequences of floods by enabling swift action before disasters occur, ultimately aiming to protect lives and livelihoods in affected areas. The plan reflects a commitment to building resilience and improving disaster response mechanisms in Somalia.

somalia.title: 'No decision yet on interim coaches’ future after Somalia clash' – Henry Asante Twum - 3News
somalia.summary: The future of interim coaches for the Ghanaian national football team remains uncertain following their recent match against Somalia. Henry Asante Twum, a spokesperson for the Ghana Football Association, stated that no decision has been made regarding the coaches' positions. The team faced criticism after the clash, which has raised questions about the coaching staff's effectiveness. Asante Twum emphasized that discussions are ongoing, and a resolution will be reached in due course. The association is considering various factors before making any announcements about the coaching situation.

somalia.title: Somalia parliament speaker accuses Kenya of harbouring terrorists - Somali Guardian
somalia.summary: Somalia's parliament speaker has accused Kenya of harboring terrorists, claiming that the country is providing a safe haven for individuals involved in militant activities against Somalia. This accusation comes amid ongoing tensions between the two nations, particularly concerning security and border issues. The speaker emphasized the need for Kenya to take responsibility for its actions and to cooperate with Somalia in combating terrorism. The remarks reflect a broader concern within Somalia regarding the influence of external actors on its security situation. The Somali government has previously expressed similar concerns, urging regional cooperation to address the threats posed by militant groups. The situation remains delicate as both countries navigate their complex relationship.

somalia.title: OIC reaffirms support for Somalia’s territorial integrity during talks in Baghdad - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has reiterated its commitment to Somalia's territorial integrity during discussions held in Baghdad. The meeting focused on various issues affecting the region, with member states expressing solidarity with Somalia amid ongoing challenges. The OIC emphasized the importance of unity and cooperation among member nations to support Somalia's stability and development. Participants highlighted the need for a collective approach to address security concerns and promote peace in the country. The reaffirmation of support comes as Somalia continues to navigate complex political and security landscapes, with the OIC pledging to assist in efforts aimed at strengthening the nation's sovereignty and territorial claims.

somalia.title: Somalia’s Civil Aviation Authority signs flight safety agreement with International Air Transport Association - The Tanzania Times
somalia.summary: Somalia’s Civil Aviation Authority has signed a flight safety agreement with the International Air Transport Association (IATA). This agreement aims to enhance aviation safety standards in Somalia and improve the overall safety of air travel in the region. The collaboration is expected to facilitate the implementation of international safety protocols and best practices in the Somali aviation sector. IATA's support will assist Somalia in developing its aviation infrastructure and regulatory framework, ultimately contributing to the growth of the country's air transport industry. The agreement marks a significant step towards ensuring safer skies for both domestic and international flights operating in and out of Somalia.

somalia.title: Heartbreak for Ocean Stars as Uganda Win CECAFA Final Shootout - FTL Somalia
somalia.summary: In a dramatic CECAFA final, Uganda triumphed over the Ocean Stars in a penalty shootout, leaving the Somali team heartbroken. The match, held in a tense atmosphere, ended in a 1-1 draw after regulation and extra time, leading to the decisive penalties. Uganda showcased composure under pressure, converting all their spot-kicks, while the Ocean Stars struggled, missing crucial penalties. This victory marks Uganda's significant achievement in the regional tournament, while Somalia's hopes for a first CECAFA title were dashed. The match highlighted the growing competitiveness of football in the region, with both teams displaying skill and determination throughout the tournament.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يصنع الحدث و"غربال" على موعد مع المجد - شبكة تواصل الإخبارية
football.summary: الهلال السوداني حقق إنجازًا كبيرًا في مسيرته الكروية، حيث تمكن من الوصول إلى مراحل متقدمة في المنافسات القارية. اللاعب "غربال" كان له دور بارز في هذا النجاح، حيث أظهر مهاراته العالية وأداءه المتميز في المباريات. الجماهير تتطلع إلى المزيد من الإنجازات، مع آمال كبيرة في تحقيق الألقاب. الهلال يسعى لتعزيز مكانته في الساحة الرياضية، ويبدو أن الفريق في طريقه لتحقيق المجد الذي يطمح إليه.

football.title: الهلال السوداني والسويحلي الليبي يقتربان من مجموعات دوري الأبطال - مانكيش نت
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا. جاء ذلك بعد الأداء القوي الذي قدمه الفريقان في المباريات التمهيدية. الهلال السوداني حقق نتائج إيجابية في مبارياته السابقة، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل، بينما تمكن السويحلي من تقديم عرض قوي في التصفيات. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى تحقيق النجاح في المرحلة المقبلة من البطولة، حيث تعتبر هذه المنافسة فرصة كبيرة لإظهار مهاراتهم على المستوى القاري.

football.title: الهلال السوداني والسويحلي الليبي يقتربان من دور المجموعات في دوري ابطال افريقيا - Elsport
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى دور المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا بعد أدائهما القوي في التصفيات. حيث حقق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على منافسه في مباراة الذهاب، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل. من جهة أخرى، قدم السويحلي الليبي عرضاً مميزاً في مباراته، مما يضعه في موقف جيد للتقدم في البطولة. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى تحقيق نتائج إيجابية في مباريات الإياب لضمان مكانهما في دور المجموعات، حيث تعتبر هذه المرحلة من البطولة ذات أهمية كبيرة للأندية الأفريقية.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يحسم مواجهة سيداما بونا ويقترب من التأهل الأفريقي - اخبار السودان
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزًا مهمًا على سيداما بونا الإثيوبي في مباراة ضمن تصفيات دوري أبطال أفريقيا، مما يقربه من التأهل للمرحلة التالية. انتهت المباراة بفوز الهلال بنتيجة 2-0، حيث سجل الأهداف كل من اللاعب محمد عبد الرحمن واللاعب وليد الشعلة. قدم الفريق أداءً قويًا خلال المباراة، مما ساهم في تعزيز فرصه في المنافسة على اللقب الأفريقي. بهذا الفوز، يواصل الهلال مسيرته الناجحة في البطولة ويعزز من موقفه في المجموعة.

football.title: موعد بث مواجهة الهلال وسيداما والقنوات الناقلة للقاء المرتقب اليوم - موقع رادار
football.summary: تقام اليوم مواجهة مرتقبة بين فريق الهلال وسيداما، حيث ينتظر عشاق كرة القدم هذه المباراة بفارغ الصبر. ستبدأ المباراة في تمام الساعة 8:00 مساءً بتوقيت مكة المكرمة. سيتم بث اللقاء عبر عدة قنوات، منها القناة الرياضية السعودية، بالإضافة إلى منصات البث المباشر على الإنترنت. يُعتبر هذا اللقاء مهمًا للفريقين، حيث يسعى الهلال لتحقيق الفوز لتعزيز موقفه في البطولة، بينما يأمل سيداما في تقديم أداء قوي أمام خصمهم.

football.title: موعد بث مواجهة الهلال وسيداما والقنوات الناقلة للقاء المرتقب اليوم - موقع رادار
football.summary: تستعد جماهير كرة القدم لمتابعة مواجهة الهلال وسيداما اليوم، حيث من المقرر أن تنطلق المباراة في تمام الساعة 8:00 مساءً بتوقيت مكة المكرمة. ستقام المباراة في إطار المنافسات القارية، مما يزيد من حماس المشجعين. يمكن متابعة اللقاء عبر عدة قنوات ناقلة، منها قناة "SSC" التي تمتلك حقوق البث، بالإضافة إلى منصات البث المباشر. يُتوقع أن تكون المباراة مثيرة، حيث يسعى الهلال لتحقيق الفوز وتعزيز موقفه في البطولة.

football.title: السويحلي يسقط الترجي وتعادل صنداونز.. نتائج ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا - يلاكورة
football.summary: حقق فريق السويحلي فوزًا مهمًا على الترجي التونسي في ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا، مما يعزز آماله في التأهل للدور المقبل. في مباراة أخرى، انتهت مواجهة صنداونز الجنوب أفريقي مع منافسه بالتعادل، مما يجعل الأمور مفتوحة في مباراة الإياب. تأتي هذه النتائج في إطار المنافسات القوية التي يشهدها دوري أبطال أفريقيا، حيث يسعى كل فريق لتحقيق أفضل أداء لضمان التأهل.

football.title: مدرب الهلال يتوعد سيداما ويثق في بلوغ مجموعات دوري الأبطال - winwin
football.summary: مدرب الهلال، رامون دياز، أعرب عن ثقته في قدرة فريقه على تجاوز عقبة سيداما الإثيوبي في التصفيات المؤهلة لدوري أبطال آسيا. خلال مؤتمر صحفي، أكد دياز أن الهلال يمتلك الإمكانيات اللازمة لتحقيق الفوز والتأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات. وأشار إلى أهمية المباراة وضرورة التركيز على الأداء الجيد، مشددًا على أن الفريق جاهز تمامًا لمواجهة التحديات. كما أعرب عن تفاؤله بقدرة اللاعبين على تقديم مستوى مميز يضمن لهم النجاح في هذه المرحلة الحاسمة.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يقترب من مجموعات الأبطال بثنائية.. ومولودية الجزائر في ورطة - الجمهور الإخباري
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على ضيفه مولودية الجزائر بنتيجة 2-0 في مباراة الذهاب من الدور التمهيدي لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. بهذا الانتصار، اقترب الهلال من التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات، حيث قدم أداءً قوياً واستطاع تسجيل هدفين في الشوط الثاني. في المقابل، يواجه مولودية الجزائر تحديات كبيرة بعد هذه الخسارة، مما يزيد من ضغوط الفريق قبل مباراة الإياب. يحتاج الفريق الجزائري إلى تحقيق نتيجة إيجابية في المباراة القادمة لضمان فرصه في التأهل.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يضرب في إثيوبيا ويقترب من مجموعات أبطال أفريقيا - السودان اليوم
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على مضيفه فاسيل كيتيما الإثيوبي في مباراة الذهاب من الدور التمهيدي لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. انتهت المباراة بفوز الهلال بنتيجة 2-0، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات. سجل أهداف الهلال كل من اللاعب محمد عبد الرحمن واللاعب وليد الشعلة، حيث قدم الفريق أداءً مميزاً خلال اللقاء. ومن المقرر أن تقام مباراة الإياب في السودان، حيث يسعى الهلال إلى تأكيد تفوقه وضمان التأهل. يعتبر هذا الفوز خطوة إيجابية نحو تحقيق طموحات الفريق في البطولة الأفريقية.
